name: Future Fisheries Improvement Program
summary: Twice-yearly Montana grants for on-the-ground restoration of rivers, streams and lakes to improve wild fish habitat, such as fish passage, stream channel and riparian work, with landowner approval.

steps: Talk to the area FWP fisheries biologist first

eligibility.rule: Evaluate the problem's cause, take a large-scale view and benefit the angling public
Avoid interfering with adjacent landowners' water or property rights
Demonstrate public benefits and accomplish at least one listed program goal
Budget excludes admin, travel, coordination, overhead, monitoring, studies, design-only, contingency and land purchase
Ensure riparian fencing does not adversely affect wildlife
Commits to maintain the project for at least 20 years

documents: Project plans or detailed restoration sketches
Landowner support letter, if applicant differs from landowner
Local FWP fisheries biologist statement or letter
Supplemental water leasing or water salvage questionnaire, if applicable

deadline.quote: The Summer 2026 Future Fisheries Improvement Program grant application deadline is May 15, 2026.

calls.label: Winter funding cycle
calls.recurring: Applications are due on 15 November each year (winter cycle) and 15 May (summer cycle).

status.quote: The Future Fisheries Improvement Program grant applications are due May 15 (summer cycle) and November 15 (winter cycle) of each year.

recurring.quote: The Future Fisheries Improvement Program grant applications are due May 15 (summer cycle) and November 15 (winter cycle) of each year.

pool.quote: Approximately $1 million are available each year for projects that revitalize wild fish populations.

applicant_types.quote: Any entity with a good on-the-ground project that benefits wild fish can apply for funding through the Future Fisheries Improvement Program, including (but is not limited to) landowners, anglers, civic groups, conservation districts, or governmental agencies.

geography.quote: To be eligible, projects must be completed within the state of Montana.

access.quote: Applications must be completed in entirety and signed by the applicant.

window.quote: The Future Fisheries Improvement has a summer and winter funding cycle each year.

co_finance_required.quote: Permanent irrigation diversions must have at least a 50% match.

consortium_required.quote: Any individual or group can apply.

effort.quote: Talk to your area fisheries biologist about your project idea prior to filling out an application.

Submit applications to the Future Fisheries Coordinator at the FWP headquarters in Helena at FWPFFIP@mt.gov. They must be received on or before May 15 (summer cycle) or November 15 (winter cycle) to be considered for funding.
Applications are sorted, sent to the Future Fisheries Citizen Review Panel, and posted on the Future Fisheries webpage to provide the opportunity for public review and comment.
Review Panel funding recommendations are forwarded to the Fish & Wildlife Commission for final action during their August or February meetings (corresponding to the summer and winter funding cycles).

eligibility.quote: Projects must evaluate the cause of the problem, incorporate a large-scale view of the project and surrounding area, and benefit the angling public.
Projects must have written landowner permission.

Project applicants must also affirm that work would be conducted with the approval of the landowner on whose property the project is being completed, and would not interfere with water or property rights of adjacent landowners.
Applicants must demonstrate benefits to the public and accomplish one or more of the goals listed below:
Funding cannot be used for administration, travel, coordination, overhead, monitoring, assessment or studies, design alone (must be design/build), contingency, or land acquisition.
Applications involving installation of riparian fencing must ensure the project does not adversely affect wildlife species.

co_finance.quote: Permanent irrigation diversions must have at least a 50% match.

after_award.quote: The final 10% of the grant award will not be released until the Future Fisheries Coordinator or a designated FWP representative visits the site and verifies project completion.

documents.quote: Attach itemized (line item) budget - see budget template H. Attach project location map(s) that include: Extent of the project, including context (relation to major landmark or town) Indication of public and private property Riparian buffer locations and widths (if applicable) and grazing locations I. Attach project plans: Detailed sketches or plan views with the location and proposed restoration

A plan-view map of the project site showing specific location(s) of planned restoration activities. At a minimum, a support letter from the landowner (if the applicant differs from the landowner). A statement or letter or support from the local FWP fisheries biologist.
If water leasing or water salvage is involved, attach a supplemental questionnaire (https://myfwp.mt.gov/getRepositoryFile?objectID=36110)
